evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Nicole says 'This call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes' and mentions she can 'provide you an estimate with your move,' but does NOT explicitly frame the dependable quote promise or wait for a yes before pivoting to 'what are your biggest concerns.'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Nicole: 'I'd like to ask first what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today?' — asked before any logistics probing. Mina responds with pricing and availability concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — Mina raised two concerns (pricing and availability), but Nicole did not dig deeper with follow-up questions like 'tell me more about that.' She moved directly to confirming details instead of exploring the concerns further.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — Nicole did not summarize back what she heard. She acknowledged the concerns ('I can definitely help you with that') but never reflected them as a summary.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Nicole gathered: property type (1-bed/2-bed apartment), floors (4th to 3rd), rooms, walking distances (using school-bus reference), additional stops (none), elevator access. All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not offered. Nicole never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. Nicole: 'for a typical one bedroom motive items we usually expect to see around fifteen to 25 boxes to move. Do you think you'll fall within that range?' Mina clarifies she'll have 5–10 boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Nicole: 'for a typical one bedroom apartment it usually takes around two and a half to three and a half hours to completely move locally in your case. Since you're moving from a fourth floor apartment with a bit of a long walk moving to a third floor apartment with few boxes. I will estimate this move to take around three to four hours with two movers and one truck and it's good the budget around $660 to $880.' — anchored range + personalized to her specific move (4th to 3rd floor, few boxes).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Nicole covers trip/hourly rate ($220/hr), no hidden fees (credit card, transportation, sterile, disassemble/reassembly), fuel/truck/insurance/pads/tools included, 2.5-hour minimum, and 15-minute increments. Fee transparency and commitment framing both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Nicole never asks 'Does that feel fair?' She moves directly into the Two Promises section without pausing for the customer's reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Nicole: 'we have on time guarantee if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill and the way the clock work is the time start as soon as we get on site and open the contract.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Nicole: 'we have no worries, damage coverage, we provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages' — covers $2,000 and no-deductible framing. Also states it's included (built into the rate, not an add-on).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Nicole does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm that the Two Promises answered the customer's stated concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Nicole: 'do you have any questions or anything for me?' — empty, automatic-no phrasing, not a genuine 'what's still concerning you?' check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Nicole never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or similar catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Nicole: 'would you like our help with your move?' — asked plainly with no softened out or alternative offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: True. Nicole: 'to secure a spot there's no deposit record if you have to reschedule or cancel no fees for that either' — covers no-deposit and no-cancel-fee protection.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (Friday October 16th), phone (512-239-8075), email (Mina will log the 228 @gmail.com), arrival window (8:30 AM, within 30 min), crew size (2 movers, 1 truck). Missing: full confirmation of both addresses (Nicole has them but does not re-confirm the new unit number — Mina says she doesn't know it, Nicole says to follow up later). No notes left for crew about the customer's concerns.

top_strength: Nicole systematically gathered all seven logistics details and personalized the estimate to the customer's specific move (4th-floor origin, 3rd-floor destination, few boxes), creating a credible and tailored quote.
coaching_note: Ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate and hold the silence before pivoting to Two Promises — that pause gives the customer space to object and strengthens the frame; also skip 'any questions?' and ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' instead to catch real remaining worries.
